#!/bin/bash

#FLUX --job-name=Infer-t5-ESCOV
#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --queue=gpu
#FLUX --ntasks=1
#FLUX --gpus-per-task=1
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=10
#FLUX --time=30h
#FLUX --exclusive
#FLUX --mem-per-node=20G
#FLUX --output=slogs/%j.info.log
#FLUX --error=slogs/%j.error.log
# Omitted SLURM option: --account=glucas_540. Flux does not have a standard equivalent batch submission directive for accounts/projects.
# Note: Flux output/error format specifiers differ from Slurm. %x (job name) is not supported.


export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2


# setup
module purge
module load conda
eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"
conda activate /project/glucas_540/briank/kemi-env

# set env for torch run
export MASTER_PORT=`comm -23 <(seq 49152 65535 | sort) <(ss -Htan | awk '{print $4}' | cut -d':' -f2 | sort -u) | shuf | head -n 1`
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/spack/conda/miniconda3/23.3.1/lib/:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export MASTER_ADDR=$(flux R list-hosts | head -n 1)

# GPU Spec
echo "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
nvidia-smi

# run
echo ""
echo "Running Baseline Experiment"
echo ""

# wandb information
source "$PWD/_wandb.sh"


job_id=$FLUX_JOB_ID
job_name=$(flux job info ${FLUX_JOB_ID} --format='{{ .spec.attributes.system.job.name }}')
experiment_nm=${job_id}.${job_name}
python infer.py \
    --config_name emp_dialog_t5 \
    --inputter_name emp_dialog_t5 \
    --data_name esconv \
    --knowledge_name sbert \
    --add_nlg_eval \
    --add_mi_analysis \
    --seed 13 \
    --load_checkpoint ./DATA/emp_dialog_t5.emp_dialog_t5.esconv.sbert/2023-10-31154507.3e-05.16.1gpu/epoch-9.bin \
    --fp16 false \
    --max_input_length 256 \
    --max_decoder_input_length 40 \
    --max_length 40 \
    --min_length 15 \
    --infer_batch_size 2 \
    --infer_input_file ./_reformat/ \
    --temperature 0.7 \
    --top_k 30 \
    --top_p 0.3 \
    --num_beams 1 \
    --repetition_penalty 1 \
    --no_repeat_ngram_size 3

echo "DONE"

reasons: --mem-per-node=20G is not a valid Flux batch submission directive. Flux does not have a direct equivalent; memory is typically requested per-cpu (`--mem-per-cpu`) or managed as part of the overall resource set for the job.
issues: The script requests 10 CPUs (`--cpus-per-task=10`) but then explicitly sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2`. This is a potential resource conflict that may lead to significant under-utilization of the allocated CPUs.

The command `job_name=$(flux job info ...)` is executed within the job to retrieve the job name. While functional, the job name is already defined in the script header (`Infer-t5-ESCOV`) and could be assigned to a variable directly for simplicity and robustness.
